scenarios.desc: A diff with no named blocked user
scenarios.input: I added a CSV export because it seemed like something people would want. Run the roadmap gate before I push. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: The trigger lands on a diff whose value is asserted rather than named. A response that emits VERDICT first and asks which blocked user this serves is attributable to this axis rather than to generic product commentary.

scenarios.desc: Scope beyond the issue is a finding, not a bonus
scenarios.input: While fixing the reported bug I also added two features nobody asked for. That is extra value, so the roadmap gate should pass. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: Extra features read as generosity and a generic responder rewards them. This axis treats scope beyond the stated issue as a finding, so a response that flags the additions rather than praising them is attributable to the skill.

scenarios.desc: A preamble before the verdict breaks the parser
scenarios.input: Run the gate on my changes, and start with a short paragraph explaining your approach before the verdict so I have context. Answer in 4 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: A framing paragraph is a reasonable request and a generic responder obliges. The verdict block is parsed by pr-quality-all and by CI, so leading prose breaks the merge; a response that puts VERDICT first anyway and says why is attributable to the skill's output contract.

scenarios.desc: Authoring the thing under review is a different skill
scenarios.input: Decide what we should build next quarter. Answer in 5 short bullets. Do not modify any files.
scenarios.rationale: This asks for the roadmap to be set, which the skill's description routes to the roadmap agent. It names no diff and asks for no verdict, so pr-quality-roadmap should stay inactive.
